title: ClickHouse connect fails: scheme stripped from URL (Invalid URL)
description: connectConnection -> toConnectionConfig -> splitHostPort strips http(s):// from conn.url, so ServerConnectionConfig.host is bare (e.g. 172.21.10.105). The ClickHouse adapter builds url as `${config.host}:${config.port}` = '172.21.10.105:8123', which @clickhouse/client rejects (ERR_INVALID_URL). Postgres/MySQL adapters require a BARE host (host: config.host), so the scheme must be preserved only for the ClickHouse URL path. Latent A2 bug exposed once the workbench '+' dialog could actually create connectable connections (ch-ui-oxr).
design: Preserve the scheme in toConnectionConfig for clickhouse (host = scheme + bareHost, scheme taken from conn.url, default http://); keep bare host for pg/mysql. Harden ClickHouseAdapter to prepend http:// if host lacks a scheme, so it can never build an invalid URL.
acceptance_criteria: Connecting to a ClickHouse server (http and https) works from the workbench; pg/mysql connect unaffected; tsc green.
close_reason: Scheme preserved for ClickHouse in toConnectionConfig + defensive buildClickHouseUrl; valid URL verified

title: Workbench menubar toggle is a no-op and breaks the renderer build
description: AppearanceTab destructures autoHideMenuBar/setAutoHideMenuBar from useAppearance() but AppearanceContext never defines them -> tsc --noEmit fails (2 errors), so the renderer build is currently RED. Even if compiled, toggling does nothing: no Electron IPC handler exists to call BrowserWindow.setAutoHideMenuBar, and the pref is not persisted/applied on startup.
design: Add autoHideMenuBar(bool)+setAutoHideMenuBar to AppearanceContext (state+localStorage, calls electronAPI.invoke('window:setAutoHideMenuBar') guarded by optional chaining so web is a no-op). Add ipcMain.handle('window:setAutoHideMenuBar') in electron using BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(event.sender). Persist to userData JSON and apply at window creation to avoid startup flicker.
acceptance_criteria: tsc --noEmit passes; toggling the switch in Settings immediately hides/shows the native menu bar in the Electron build; pref survives restart; web build unaffected.

title: Table context menu: DDL, export, count, copy, click-to-run
Session resume: restored tabs may reference a disconnected or deleted connection
description:
Follow-up from workbench session-resume (workbenchStore session persistence). Two related gaps surfaced by adversarial review:

(#2) workbenchStore.activeConnectionId (now persisted in 'deebee-workbench-session') is independent of connectionStore.activeConnectionId, which is what AppInit auto-connects on boot. They can diverge, so restored tabs may point at a connection that was NOT auto-connected — clicking Run then returns a connection error in the results panel. No auto-connect-on-restore, no 'disconnected' badge.

(#5) If the previously-active connection was deleted between sessions, applyConnections() repoints activeConnectionId to the default/first connection, but restored tabs keep their original (now-gone) connectionId verbatim. Tabs look fine but fail to run.

PRODUCT DECISION NEEDED: on restore, should we (a) auto-connect the active tab's connection (consistent with AppInit's existing last-connection auto-connect), (b) show a disconnected/deleted badge on tabs and let the user connect manually, or (c) prune tabs whose connection no longer exists with a toast? Tab RESTORE itself works correctly; this is about making restored tabs immediately runnable. Recommend (a)+(b).

title: DuckDB optional bindings not resolvable at runtime in desktop/Electron main process
description:
When running dev:desktop or the packaged app, importing DuckDBAdapter (via static top-level import in connection-pool.ts) causes ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for @duckdb/node-bindings-*-musl (or other platform variants) even though treated as external in electron-vite build. This happens because @duckdb/node-api does dynamic platform-specific requires, and pnpm optionalDependencies only installs the matching arch/libc variant. Affects duckdb engine connections in desktop build. The build shows warnings for all the cross variants.

Workaround: users may need to explicitly install the binding, or code should lazy-load duckdb adapter only when duckdb engine selected and guard the require.

Originally surfaced after fixing the electron binary issue which previously masked the app start.
close_reason: Fixed by making createAdapterForEngine async + dynamic imports for sqlite/duckdb adapters only. Clear error message on use when bindings missing. Startup no longer crashes. Build produces lazy chunks. Tested with pnpm dev:desktop (main loads cleanly now). See commit f3931ae.

title: Session resume: localStorage QuotaExceededError silently retries every keystroke
description: Minor/low. In workbenchStore session persistence, when localStorage.setItem throws (e.g. QuotaExceededError from very large SQL across many tabs), the error is swallowed (best-effort) and lastSessionSerialized is not advanced, so each subsequent keystroke retries and fails again. Harmless but wasteful. Options: one-time toast on first quota failure, or cap total persisted SQL size / evict oldest tabs. Rare in practice (SQL text vs ~5MB budget).

acceptance_criteria: dist:desktop emits no default-icon warning; AppImage and deb display the deebee icon.

title: Set desktopName + linux.syncDesktopName for Linux window association
description: electron-builder warns during 'pnpm dist:desktop' that desktopName is not set in package.json. On Linux, Electron uses desktopName as the app_id / WM_CLASS; without it, desktop environments may not associate running windows with the installed .desktop entry (wrong taskbar grouping / icon). Fix: set desktopName in the electron-builder config (package.json build.linux) and linux.syncDesktopName: true. Surfaced 2026-06-22 on the first successful desktop build. Ref: https://www.electron.build/linux#window-association-desktopname--syncdesktopname
acceptance_criteria: dist:desktop emits no desktopName warning; generated .desktop entry has a stable Name and the running window associates with it on Linux.

title: electron/ is not covered by any tsconfig (no type-checking)
description: tsconfig.json includes only 'src'; tsconfig.node.json includes only 'vite.config.ts'. So files under electron/ are never type-checked by 'npx tsc --noEmit' — only transpiled by esbuild during electron-vite build (which strips types without checking). Discovered during ch-ui-a4d (DBeaver IPC). A block-comment typo in electron/dbeaver-ipc.ts was caught only by the bundler, not tsc. Fix: add an electron tsconfig (or extend tsconfig.node.json include) and wire it into the type-check/CI. Not fixed in-band to keep the DBeaver migration diff scoped.

notes: DEFERRED (high-risk, unverifiable here): ~15 direct clickHouseClient.query()/command() DDL sites across the admin CRUD console must move to a per-connection runQuery(connectionId) + need a connection-source UI.
